html:
Ask any Greer host which review comment stings most and a lot will say the same thing: "found hair on the floor." Floors, baseboards and the edges of rooms are where a turnover is judged, because guests walk in, look down and notice. This article covers how we handle floors for Airbnb cleaning in Greer, including the baseboards and corners that a quick vacuum leaves behind.

Start with the floor type, not the mop

Rentals around Greer mix hardwood, laminate, tile and carpet, sometimes in the same hallway. The tool and the method change for each:

FloorHow we clean itWhat to watch
Hardwood and laminateVacuum or dry microfiber first, then a lightly damp mopToo much water lifts seams and leaves streaks
Tile and groutVacuum, then mop with a fresh cloth headGrout lines hold grime and show in photos
Carpet and rugsSlow, overlapping passesPet hair and food crumbs near the sofa
Entry matsShake, vacuum, spot cleanRed clay tracked in from the yard

Our included floor work is vacuuming and mopping throughout the property. If a floor needs more than that, such as a stained rug, we will say so at the estimate rather than promise it and miss.

Why Upstate floors get dirty in a particular way

Greenville and Spartanburg counties sit on red clay. After a rainy week, guests walk it into the entry, and it dries into a fine orange dust that spreads when you mop too early. In spring the pollen adds a yellow layer on porch floors and door thresholds. In humid summer months, bare feet leave marks on tile. Knowing this changes the order: we vacuum or sweep first so the mop is not pushing a paste around.

The edges guests actually see

A floor is only as clean as its borders. Here is the checklist we run along the edge of each room:

  • Baseboards wiped along the full length, especially behind doors
  • Corners and the gap where the floor meets the wall, where dust lines build up
  • Under and behind the bed, nightstands and the sofa
  • The track of a sliding patio door
  • Door thresholds and the strip under the front door
  • Vent covers and the floor right below them
  • The edge of the stairs, if the house has them

Baseboards deserve a special mention. In a rental, they pick up scuffs from luggage and suitcase wheels, and they hold the hair that settles at the wall. Wiping them takes a minute per room and changes how the whole space looks in a photo.

Our floor order in a turnover

  1. Pull rugs and light furniture so nothing hides a spot.
  2. Dust baseboards and edges before the floor, so debris falls onto a floor we have not cleaned yet.
  3. Vacuum each room, working toward the door.
  4. Mop from the farthest room back toward the exit, kitchen and bathrooms last.
  5. Replace rugs and furniture, then do a final walk to catch footprints.

Doing the kitchen floor near the end matters, since cooking residue is the stickiest. For what happens in that room, our post on Airbnb cleaning in Greer for bedrooms and closets follows the same room-by-room logic, and for hosts in a neighboring town, the turnover checklist for Fountain Inn hosts is a useful comparison.

What a floor report tells you

Because every turnover ends with a damage and missing-item report with photos, the floors are documented too. A gouge from a dragged suitcase, a burn mark near a fireplace or a stain on a rug shows up in the photos with the date, and that helps if you need to follow up with a guest or the platform. Hosts who live out of town tell us they like this part most, since they can see the property without driving to Greer. If you want to understand how the same method works across a whole property, Airbnb cleaning in Greer walks through the service from check-out to staging.

One more habit worth mentioning: we check the floor again after the beds are made and the trash is out. Pulling linens and bags across a clean floor leaves lint and crumbs, and a final pass takes only a few minutes. It is also when we see whether a bedside rug is crooked or a chair leg has left a mark, so the room matches your listing photos before we lock up. Guests who arrive to a floor that looks as clean as the picture rarely mention it, and that is exactly the result a host wants.

Floors are usually the last big task in a turnover, and they set the pace for the finish. A small cottage and a five-bedroom home near SC-101 are very different jobs, which is why we want to see the property first. For a booking this week, text (864) 666-8520.

Small things hosts can do

  • Put a boot tray and a doormat inside and outside the front door.
  • Choose washable rugs over shag rugs.
  • Tell us about floors with a special finish so we use the right products.
  • Keep furniture legs padded, which keeps floor scuffs down and baseboards cleaner.

faqs: Do you wipe baseboards during every Airbnb turnover?

Baseboards and door frames are part of how we finish the edges of a room. Heavy build-up that has been there for months is better handled with a deeper clean, and we will point that out at the estimate.
Can you clean hardwood floors without damaging them?
Yes. We vacuum or dry-clean first and use a lightly damp mop, so the floor is not soaked. Tell us about any special finish ahead of time.
How do you deal with red clay tracked in by guests?
We remove the loose dirt with a vacuum or sweep before mopping, so the mop does not smear it. A mat inside the door helps cut down how much comes in.
